# Independent audit: integral Jensen filter and simplex depth

The graph source is
`candidate 5c9190df7c42c598`.
Its exact verifier is
`supporting computation verify_integral_jensen_graph_filter_counterexample.py`.

**Graph theorem verdict: PASS.** The verifier reruns with plain
Python and returns PASS. The checks below independently justify
the steps that are not merely finite arithmetic.

## 1. Actual integer support and every Jensen relation

The nine displayed inequalities imply 0<=y<=x<=2 and 0<=z<=2.
Summing the third and eighth inequalities gives the upper bound
on z. Thus checking all 27 integer points in that box is exhaustive.
The exact verifier also intersects every independent triple of
boundary planes and checks feasibility. Its feasible vertex set
is precisely the nine listed points other than p_2 and p_8. Each
displayed inequality has a two-dimensional face, so none of the
minimal-face arguments relies on a spurious inequality. The strict
interior test point and boundedness establish a full convex body.

At p_2 only y=0 is active. At p_8 only x=2 is active. Every other
integer point is a vertex, and every point lies on some facet.
Hence the support is lattice-convex and hollow as stated.

Any convex representation of a point in the relative interior of
a face uses only points on that face: equality in every active
support inequality forces equality at every positive-weight source.
On the entire sampled y=0 face, g equals (3-x-z)/2. On the entire
sampled x=2 face it equals zero. Therefore all anchored convex
representations at the only two nonvertices preserve g. Vertex
representations are trivial. This proves g belongs to L(P), without
replacing the all-representation condition by a few checked pairs.

The four zero-height points p_3,p_4,p_5,p_6 form an affine basis of
R^3, while g(p_0)=1, so ordinary global affine interpolation is
impossible. The two five-point planar minimal faces impose two
independent equations each, sharing only p_6. Their total relation
rank is four; thus the optional dimension count dim L(P)=7 also
checks. It is not needed for the Helly counterexample.

## 2. Exact integer graph and critical nine-point set

An integer point (p,t) of conv(T) projects into conv(P) intersect
Z^3=P. Jensen affinity then forces t=g(p). The unique fractional
height is g(p_2)=1/2, so the graph has exactly its claimed ten
integer points and no extras. This argument is valid even when
the representing convex combination does not use p itself.

Every listed normal exposes its specified W point by a strict
unit gap from the other eight W points. The separate inequality
y+z<=2 excludes p_9, whose value is three. Therefore each W point
is omitted by its own deletion hull and p_9 is omitted by every
deletion hull. Conversely, deleting any one hull from the family
leaves its omitted W point in all remaining hulls. This is a
minimal nine-member T-infeasible family, proving h(T)>=9.

The two disjoint pairs (p_0,p_6) and (p_1,p_3) have midpoint p_2.
After any one W point is removed, one entire pair remains. Both
lifted midpoint heights are exactly 1/2. Thus the original-base
deletion kernel contains p_2 and no other P point, but its actual
graph witness is removed by the integer-height requirement.

The graph of W is full dimensional in R^4: its four independent
zero-height points span a three-dimensional affine hyperplane,
and p_0 has height one. The exposing normals, outlier exclusion,
and fractional p_2 height show that its only integer points are
its nine vertices. The verifier's independent exact facet and
box enumeration confirms the same statement.

## 3. Exact Helly upper bound

For completeness, let a minimal infeasible family have ten members.
Choose a T point lying in all but each respective member. Such
witnesses are distinct: the witness for one omitted set lies in
every other set and cannot equal that other set's witness. Since
T has ten points, the witnesses enumerate all of T. Each family
member therefore contains the convex hull of all witnesses but
its own. If any witness belongs to the convex hull of the others,
it lies in every family member, a contradiction.

But the graph of p_8 is the midpoint of the graphs of p_7 and p_9,
so T is not in convex position. A critical ten-member family is
impossible. Every T-infeasible family has an infeasible subfamily
of at most ten members, by choosing one excluding set for each
point of T. Hence h(T)<=9. Combining the two inequalities proves
the exact value h(T)=9, rather than merely a lower bound.

The auxiliary integer rank is four, while the original coarse rank
is three. The example falsifies the asserted automatic bound 2^3
for the filtered graph; it does not contradict integer Helly in
rank four or an OC inequality at the actual integer rank.

## 4. Full-dimensional simplex-fiber source

Also audited in full:
`candidate 3b375252ca398671`
and `supporting computation verify_collapsed_graph_simplex_depth.py`.

**Simplex depth theorem verdict: PASS.** The verifier reruns under
`work/math-venv/bin/python` and returns PASS. SymPy is used only for
the exact rank and derivative cross-checks; the displayed geometric
and calculus proofs establish the all-dimensional statements.

The source uses the standard full s-simplex K, which contains its
chosen point k_0=0. Put K at all nine W graph bases and {0} at the
outlier graph base p_9. Since the W graph has affine dimension four
and any one positive fiber supplies all s independent vertical
directions, the hull is full dimensional in R^(4+s).

Its coarse projection is conv(P): all vertices of that polytope
are included among W and p_9, and the excluded p_2 is already a
midpoint of W sources. Jensen affinity forces every integer coarse
fiber to lie at its single actual height g(p). At a W point the
continuous fiber contains its supplied K and is contained in K,
because every generating continuous point lies in K. Thus the
fiber is exactly K. The outlier is exposed by y+z and has exactly
the singleton generating fiber. The fractional p_2 also has fiber
K, by either equal-K midpoint pair, but its height is 1/2, so it
is NOT an original fine lattice fiber. The graph lemma excludes
every other possible fine integer base.

This proves all asserted fiber identities, including the geometric
presence of the unsampled coarse fiber. All generators belong to
the actual fine mixed set, so its convex hull is exactly the full
source body. The intrinsic fine measure is H_s and has total 9V;
the outlier point has zero mass because s>=1. All full coarse
(s+1)-volumes vanish, as claimed.

## 5. Matching all-cap lower bound and finite upper cover

At any of the nine own-simplex centroids, every original containing
ambient closed halfspace captures at least Gamma_s V from that
fiber alone, by ordinary continuous Grunbaum. A restriction with
zero continuous normal contains the whole own fiber and creates
no exception. This gives normalized depth at least Gamma_s/9.

For the upper bound, the barycentric caps lambda_r>=1/(s+1)
cover K and each has exactly Gamma_s V volume. The source's fixed
tilt two makes the margin at every other positive fiber at most

    1-1/(s+1)-2 < 0,

because the exposing base gap is at least one. Thus each lifted
cap has exactly the asserted mass. A cap may contain the outlier
point, which has zero H_s mass; it need not be excluded by these
particular normals. The separate cap y+z>=3 isolates that point,
has mass zero, and completes the cover of the ENTIRE mixed set.

This finite family proves an upper bound at every possible center,
including boundary points of the positive simplices and the
outlier. Together with the centroid lower bound it proves the
exact global maximum Gamma_s/9. No inference from selected cap
directions to all directions, or from a numerical cap minimization,
is needed.

## 6. Gamma comparison and precise scope

For F(t)=log Gamma_t=t log(t/(t+1)), direct differentiation gives
F''(t)=1/[t(t+1)^2]>0 for t>0. Therefore
F(t+1)-F(t)=integral_t^(t+1) F'(v)dv is strictly increasing.
At t=1 its exponential is Gamma_2/Gamma_1=8/9. Consequently

    Gamma_s/9 < Gamma_(s+1)/8   for every integer s>=2,

with equality at s=1. The exact s=2 gap is 139/41472. This proves
the claimed strict comparison in all dimensions, beyond the finite
range verified arithmetically.

The actual integer rank is FOUR, whose OC target is Gamma_s/16,
strictly below the constructed depth. Deleting fine integrality
admits the additional positive p_2 fiber and changes the measure.
The example therefore refutes automatic depth-preserving rank
deletion in the zero-coarse-volume regime, not OC itself and not a
theorem about the different measure after the deletion.
